title: Localization uniqueness promotes affine generator coherence
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative local ring and let $C$ be its maximal-ideal adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], with structural homomorphism $\varphi:A\to C$. Let $U\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$ be open, $q:Y\to U$ and $s:E\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ morphisms of schemes, and $D$ a supplied overlap identification [def-sbc-punctured-completion-matching-sections]. Let $t\in\mathbb N$, $f:\operatorname{Fin}(t)\to A$, and suppose $D(f_i)\subseteq U$ and $V_i=(q\circ U.\iota)^{-1}D(f_i)$ is affine for every $i$. Put $O=Y\times_U(\operatorname{Spec}C|_U)$ and $p:O\to Y$ its projection. Suppose $T$ is any system of transition and section equivalences satisfying the scalar and restriction formulas [lem-sbc-punctured-completion-affine-chart-transitions]. Its transition maps satisfy the square and cocycle equalities of linear maps in [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data] on every element of the appropriate iterated localized module. In particular these maps, together with $T$'s modules, are formal glueing data. No new section identifications are selected.

proof.text: apply the generator-coherence theorem to obtain equality on the original module elements. Multiplication by each power of f_j is invertible on M_j, since M_j is a module over A_(f_j). Map these invertible endomorphisms through localization and scalar extension; they remain invertible. Consequently both f_i and f_j act invertibly on the target C tensor_A (M_j)_(f_i). Apply the universal property of localization first at f_j and then at f_i: to compare the square paths it suffices to evaluate them on (m'/1)/1, which is exactly the first generator equation. Similarly f_k acts invertibly on M_k, hence on its two localizations. Powers of f_j act invertibly by the outer localization. Two applications of localization uniqueness reduce the cocycle paths to their values on (m/1)/1, given by the second generator equation. This proof constructs no geometric objects and needs no flatness. With t=0 all equalities are vacuous; with zero principal opens the same universal property applies to zero modules.

lean.statement:
theorem affine_chart_transition_coherence
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    {U : (Spec (.of A)).Opens}
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} {q : Y ⟶ U.toScheme}
    {E : Scheme.{u}} {s : E ⟶ Spec
      (.of (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A))}
    (D : CompletionGluingData A U q E s) (t : ℕ) (f : Fin t → A)
    (hf : ∀ i, PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen (f i) ≤ U)
    (hV : ∀ i, IsAffineOpen ((q ≫ U.ι) ⁻¹ᵁ PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen (f i)))
    (T : AffineChartTransitions D t f) :
    let C := AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A
    let φ := algebraMap A C
    let F := T.F
    (∀ i j : Fin t,
      (FormalGlueing.extendMapR φ (F.alpha_overlap i j).toLinearMap).comp
          ((FormalGlueing.compare φ (f j) (FormalGlueing.piece (f i) (F.M i))).comp
            (FormalGlueing.localMap (f j) (F.alpha i).toLinearMap)) =
        (FormalGlueing.compare φ (f i) (FormalGlueing.piece (f j) (F.M j))).comp
          ((FormalGlueing.localMap (f i) (F.alpha j).toLinearMap).comp
            (FormalGlueing.swap (f i) (f j) (FormalGlueing.restrict φ F.M')))) ∧
    (∀ i j k : Fin t,
      (FormalGlueing.localMap (f i) (F.alpha_overlap j k).toLinearMap).comp
          ((FormalGlueing.swap (f i) (f k) (FormalGlueing.piece (f j) (F.M j))).comp
            (FormalGlueing.localMap (f k) (F.alpha_overlap i j).toLinearMap)) =
        (FormalGlueing.swap (f i) (f j) (FormalGlueing.piece (f k) (F.M k))).comp
          ((FormalGlueing.localMap (f j) (F.alpha_overlap i k).toLinearMap).comp
            (FormalGlueing.swap (f j) (f k) (FormalGlueing.piece (f i) (F.M i)))))
